The harness threw the exception away, so the cause had to be inferred from file timestamps.

CHANGE `run_rows` (the `--run` mode) in opening_condition_v2.py:
1. Every failed call is recorded in a top-level list `failed_calls`: {call_index, thing_id, sample, error_type (the exception class name), error (str(error) truncated to 300 characters, with any value of the CLOUDFLARE_WORKER_TOKEN environment variable replaced by "<redacted>"), status (the HTTP status if any, else null)}.
2. A call is a TIMEOUT when the exception or its cause/context chain contains a TimeoutError or socket.timeout instance, or the hedged-request timeout error type defined in storygame/runtime/hedged_request.py (read that module to find what it raises); decide by exception type, never by parsing message text. A timed-out sample is NOT a stop: record it and keep going with the next planned call. After all planned calls, retry each timed-out sample ONCE, in order. A sample that fails again stays missing.
3. Stop the run (stop_reason as now, via `_stop_reason`) on any non-timeout error, and stop with stop_reason "three_consecutive_failures" after 3 consecutive failed calls of any kind.
4. Count every HTTP attempt (first tries and retries) against --max-calls; the planned 40 plus retries must fit; refuse up front only when the planned first-try count exceeds --max-calls (so --max-calls 44 allows 4 retries; never send more than --max-calls requests). If the cap is hit before all retries, stop_reason "max_calls".
5. stop_reason is None only when every planned (thing, sample) has a row. Rows keep their current fields; a retried sample's row records `attempt: 2` (first-try rows `attempt: 1`). Rows stay sorted by call order as sent. The token estimate and USD ceiling include the extra calls allowed by --max-calls (use max-calls, not the planned count, for the ceiling) so the ceiling check is conservative.
